findings.title: FLT Investigating Cyber Security Incident (statement to the Australian Securities Exchange)
findings.summary_md: The ASX statement, board-authorised and dated 26 November 2026, says Flight Centre Travel Group is investigating unusual activity in a third-party accommodation booking system used by the Flight Centre brand, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout and some independent agents, and that flight bookings and corporate travel bookings are not impacted. The company says a significant number of customer records may have been accessed by unknown persons but that it is not clear how many were actually extracted from the third-party system. Most accessed records are customer names with basic travel information, while a very small percentage is believed to include limited passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, or in rare cases health or mobility information, and no credit card, payment or bank account access has been identified. Containment described in the filing includes enhanced security and detection on affected systems, changed authentication keys and credentials, increased monitoring, notification of authorities and engagement of Mandiant.

findings.title: Hacked! Flight Centre Travel Group discloses data breach; "significant number" of customers impacted
findings.summary_md: Cyber Daily reports the company's 26 November ASX filing, naming Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout and some independent agents as the brands using the affected accommodation system while flight and corporate travel bookings are unaffected. It quotes the disclosure that a significant number of records may have been accessed but that the number extracted is unknown. The article records the split in data types, mostly names and basic travel information with a small percentage of passport details, email addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth, and states the company does not believe bank or credit card data was accessed.

findings.title: Travel giant Flight Centre hit by cyber attack with customer passport details potentially exposed
findings.summary_md: 7NEWS reports the incident from the Thursday ASX statement, listing Travel Associates, Cruiseabout and some independent agents among the affected brands with flight and corporate travel bookings unaffected. It quotes the disclosure that most records hold only names and basic travel information and that a very small percentage may include limited passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates or in rare cases health or mobility information. The article states the company said no credit card, payment or bank account details were accessed and that leisure brands continue to operate.

findings.title: FAQ: Investigating unusual activity in our third-party booking system (Travel Associates)
findings.summary_md: Travel Associates, a Flight Centre Travel Group leisure brand, published a customer FAQ it states is updated as of 15:30 AEST on 26 November 2026. It says the parent company is investigating unusual activity in a third-party booking system used by some leisure brands including Travel Associates, confirms Mandiant is engaged, and repeats that a significant number of customer records may have been accessed while the number extracted is unknown. The FAQ says the company does not believe credit card, bank or other payment details were accessed but that this position may change, tells customers not to click links or share personal information in unexpected messages, and directs inquiries to databreach@travelassociates.com.

findings.title: Passport information may have been exposed in Flight Centre cyber incident
findings.summary_md: SBS News reports that Flight Centre is investigating a data breach at one of its booking providers that may have exposed customer passport information, citing the statement to the ASX on Thursday. It quotes the company saying it is still working with the third-party vendor and its cyber security incident response partner to understand the nature and extent of the activity. Flight bookings and corporate travel bookings were not affected, and the company said a significant number of customer records were believed accessed while the number actually extracted was unknown.
